We are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Data Engineer to join our dynamic Data and Analytics team. Reporting to the Head of Data and Analytics, you will play a pivotal role in transforming raw data into actionable insights that drive strategic business decisions. This position requires a strong analytical mindset, exceptional problem-solving skills, and the ability to effectively communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. The position is more than just a “warehouse developer” role. You will work cross-functionally with various departments—to understand their workflows, model their data, and build the “connective tissue” that makes the business move faster. You will be responsible for the end-to-end lifecycle of a data product: from identifying a business need to building the dbt models and ensuring that transformed data is accessible where it’s needed most. Key Responsibilities Ownership of the Modern Data Stack (dbt & BigQuery) Act as a lead developer for our dbt project. Build performant, modular, and well-tested models that turn data into a reliable “Source of Truth.” Apply software engineering rigor to the data stack: version control (Git), documentation, unit testing, and CI/CD. Cross-Functional Automation & Intelligence Partner with business leads across the company to identify manual processes that can be streamlined through data automation. Bridge the gap between the warehouse and the business by “closing the loop”—ensuring data isn’t just sitting in a dashboard but is actively driving operational tools and decision-making. AI Integration: Leverage AI tools and LLMs to accelerate development cycles, automate documentation, and explore new ways to enhance data quality. Stakeholder Engagement Act as a consultant to business leads. Don’t just “take tickets”—understand the underlying business logic and propose better ways to structure data. Translate loosely defined business requirements into robust, automated technical solutions. Data Quality Advocacy: Work closely with stakeholders to define data quality standards and establish feedback loops that ensure data captured in upstream systems is accurate, complete, and fit for purpose. What are we looking for Essential Skills and Experience 3+ years of experience in a high-growth data environment (Analytics Engineer, Data Engineer, or Technical Data Analyst). Modern Data Stack Specialist: Deep, practical knowledge of dbt and cloud warehouses (we use BigQuery, but the experience is very transferrable). Expert-level SQL: You write complex, clean, and performant queries. Python Literacy: Not a software developer, but you must be comfortable reading code, writing scripts for data manipulation, and handling API. AI Comfort: You are an “AI-first” builder who is comfortable using AI tools (e.g., Cursor, GitHub Copilot, LLMs) to write code faster, debug, and stay ahead of the curve. Ownership Mindset: You are comfortable working independently, managing your own roadmap, and taking accountability for the entire warehouse architecture. Exceptional Communication: You can walk into a room with a non-technical team, understand their pain points, and explain your technical solution in plain English. Desired Skills and Experience: Workflow Automation: Experience with tools like n8n, Zapier, or similar automation platforms. BI/Semantic Platforms: Experience with Looker, Thoughtspot, or similar. Industry Context: Experience in Payments, FinTech, Banking, or Cryptocurrency. Reverse ETL: Familiarity with moving data from the warehouse back into SaaS tools. So, what’s in it for you? Our people are constantly striving to be the best through operational excellence. The professional development and learning opportunities create an agile, hardworking, conscientious, and knowledgeable team. The opportunities for personal growth are exponential. You grow as the business grows. The roles and responsibilities are broad and ever-changing, and the dynamism of BCB keeps you engaged and highly motivated. You deposit tokens, set reward amounts, and the protocol handles distribution automatically when users complete qualifying actions.How do you prevent bots and Sybils?We use a combination of on-chain verification, allowlists, and integration with identity providers like World ID to ensure rewards go to real users. Any standard wallet (MetaMask, Rainbow, Coinbase Wallet, etc.) can be used to claim rewards.What's RewardKit vs the Headless SDK?RewardKit is a drop-in widget for quickly embedding rewards UI in your app. The Headless SDK gives you full control over the user experience while using Boost primitives for the backend.How do we measure ROI / Return on Incentive Spend?The dashboard tracks key metrics like cost per acquisition, retention rates, and transaction volume driven by your campaigns. Compare against benchmarks to optimize spend.How fast can we go from zero to live?Most teams deploy their first Boost within 30 minutes using templates. Custom integrations with the SDK typically take a few hours to a day.Compliance and KYC/AML?Boost provides tools to integrate with compliance providers. We take on problems that matter – technically demanding, consequential, and often unsolved. We move fast without cutting corners, and we hold each other to a high standard without letting ego get in the way. Across disciplines, time zones, and five global offices, communication and trust are how we get things done. We share what we learn, own what we break, and celebrate what we build together. Where is your interest? Client experience You are the bridge between our technology and the institutions reshaping global finance. You work directly with clients to design, build, and implement solutions. Go-to-market Sales, client experience, and technical support. You shape how DA goes to market, identify where we should play, and sell a genuine paradigm shift in how financial institutions transact. Marketing You build the DA brand and shape how the market understands our role in the Canton ecosystem. Ops functions Finance, Legal, Operations, People & Workplaces, IT & Security, DA runs because of you. You're the infrastructure that lets everyone else move fast, operate with integrity, and do their best work. Product & engineering This is where Canton is built. You work on distributed systems, privacy-preserving protocols, smart contract design in Daml, and programming language theory, often all at once. Technical support You diagnose complex issues across distributed systems, advise on implementation, and make sure our customers can do what they came to DA to do. Global benefits Work-life flexibility Our benefits are designed to support flexibility, well-being, and the realities of life outside the office. Highlights include: 20 days of paid time off (PTO) accrued each year and unlimited sick time 3 Summer Fridays and a full office closure at the end of each year Paid parental leave up to 14 weeks for the primary caregiver and up to 6 weeks for the secondary caregiver Growth & learning We're building infrastructure that didn't exist before, and that's one of the best learning environments there is. You'll be challenged by the work itself, stretched by the people around you, and given the space and support to keep growing as the company does. We invest in your development deliberately: dedicated time to focus on your growth, access to external learning and certifications, and a culture where sharing what you know is part of how we win together. As DA scales, so will our investment in this work. We’re building something that matches our ambition. Our hiring process Every role is different, but here's what you can generally expect: Talent Acquisition A conversation to learn about each other: your background, interests, and what you're looking for next. Hiring Manager A deeper dive into the role, the team, and what success looks like at DA. Team Conversations Time with the people you'd work with, so both sides get a sense of fit. Skills Assessment Depending on the role, a practical exercise, case study, or portfolio walkthrough. Offer If it's a strong mutual fit, we'll move quickly. If the timing isn't right, we'll stay in touch. Life at Digital Asset “At DA, I've had the pleasure of working with some of the brightest and most thoughtful people I've ever met. DA (Digital Asset) Company Mission & Team | About DA Use Cases Back Asset Tokenization Collateral Mobility Onchain payments Wallets & Custody What We Do Back What We Do DA Registry Developers Back Docs Training & certification Company Back About us Newsroom Media Resources Careers Trust Center Partners Brand & Trademark Guidelines Contact us Insights Close Contact Us Contact Us Bringing Every Financial Asset Onchain Our mission is to bring financial assets onchain with the privacy, control and trust that global markets require ScrollBelow The DA Story DA was founded on a simple belief: financial assets should move at internet speed.Crypto began by imagining finance from the outside. DA started from within it. We believed blockchain could make markets faster, more connected and more productive — but only if it could meet the privacy, control and trust global finance requires. For more than a decade, we worked alongside leading financial institutions to understand where systems break, where assets get stuck and what production-grade infrastructure truly demands. Those lessons shaped Daml, our smart contract language, and became the foundation for Canton. Canton is where finance flows: the only public blockchain with the configurable privacy, controls and composability to work for real capital markets. Today, DA helps market leaders put Canton to work. With products, services and source-level understanding of the network we built, we help institutions move from onchain ambition to business impact. Digital Asset milestones 2026 $355 million funding round led by a16z crypto 2026 Société Générale becomes Super Validator on Canton 2026 HQLAᵡ announces investments from Digital Asset and Broadridge Financial to Support Growth on Canton 2026 Launch of digital collateral management PoC with Mizuho, Nomura, and the Japan Securities Clearing Corporation (JSCC) 2026 HSBC conducts tokenized deposit pilot on Canton 2026 Visa becomes Super Validator on Canton 2025 DA and DTCC Partner to Tokenize DTC-Custodied U.S. Treasury Securities on Canton 2025 Strategic Investments from BNY, iCapital, Nasdaq, and S&P Global 2025 Franklin Templeton’s Benji Technology Platform Expands to Canton 2025 $135 million fundraise to accelerate adoption on Canton 2025 Euroclear partners with Canton for Global Collateral Network 2025 Canton Network wins Global Custodian Digital Asset Initiative 3rd year in a row 2024 DTCC, Euroclear test the Canton Network & iCapital launch iDLT 2024 Canton Network public L1 MainNet (Global Synchronizer) launched 2023 Canton Network launched alongside 30+ market participants 2023 HKEX launches Synapse & Eleox go live 2022 Goldman Sachs DAP & Versana go live 2021 Broadridge DLR and Deutsche Borse D7 go live 2021 Series D growth round led by 7RIDGE and Eldridge Industries 2020 Series C round with VMware, Salesforce, and Samsung Ventures 2019 Daml open sourced 2018 Series B led by private family office 2016 Series A led by JP Morgan Chase 2016 Acquired Blockstack and Elevence Digital Finance 2015 Acquired Bits of Proof and Hyperledger 2014 Digital Asset is founded The world's most innovative enterprises are working with us Our leadership Yuval Rooz Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer Yuval Rooz Yuval is a visionary leader at the intersection of finance and technology. Yuval co-founded Digital Asset in 2014 to harness the promise of blockchain technology to create an open financial network where value flows as freely as information on the internet. As a Co-Founder and CEO of Digital Asset, Yuval has been instrumental in reshaping global finance by merging traditional systems with the power of decentralized technology. Yuval played a pivotal role in the formation of the Canton Network, the only public layer-one blockchain with privacy. He is also a Board Member and Treasurer of the Global Synchronizer Foundation, which he helped to create with the support of the Linux Foundation, to bring fair and transparent decentralized governance and organizational neutrality to the adoption and evolution of the Canton Network. Yuval is a member of the Digital Asset Markets subcommittee of the U.S. Commodities Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Global Market Advisory Committee and serves on the Board of Directors of the Global Blockchain Business Council, a leading industry association for the blockchain technology ecosystem. He has also testified before the U.S. House Committee on Financial Services Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology and Inclusion. Before founding Digital Asset, Yuval gained extensive experience in finance and technology, holding key positions at Citadel and DRW Trading, where he managed an algorithmic trading desk and helped launch DRW Venture Capital. Eric Saraniecki Co-Founder and Head of Network Strategy Co-Founder and Head of Network Strategy Eric Saraniecki Eric Saraniecki is co-founder and head of network strategy at Digital Asset, the organization supporting the Canton Network, focusing on strategic direction and helping build the network’s technological foundation and relationships with large institutions. Previously, he worked at DRW Trading Group as a trader, where he built and managed a trading desk focused on low-liquid commodities—a market that demands sharp analysis, strict risk management and a smart strategy. From there, he co-founded Cumberland Mining, which grew to become one of the largest liquidity providers in the crypto market. His systemic thinking, shaped by years of dealing with illiquid assets, led him to view Bitcoin as an asset with speculative opportunities and a driver of a powerful new market that required more structure and liquidity. In his current role, he gives particular focus to ensuring interoperability between applications, maintaining data privacy at the institutional level and building a network architecture that can be used by banks, clearing houses and asset managers. Shaul Kfir Co-Founder and Head of Strategic Initiatives Co-Founder and Head of Strategic Initiatives Shaul Kfir Shaul is a Co-Founder, head of strategic initiatives of Digital Asset, and a software engineer with deep roots in research cryptography. He is one of the original co-authors of libsnark, the seminal zkSNARK library that brought zero-knowledge proofs to blockchains. He holds degrees in Physics and Computer Science (cum laude) from the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology. Shaul previously conducted research at the Succinct Computational Integrity and Privacy Research Lab and served as a visiting scientist at MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Lab, where he worked under Turing Award winner Ron Rivest. Earlier in his career, he served as a Lieutenant Commander in the Israeli Navy, graduating first in his class from the Israeli Naval Academy. Edward Newman Chief Information Security Officer Chief Information Security Officer Edward Newman Edward spent more than 20 years as a senior engineering manager at leading global financial services firms, including Merrill Lynch and Goldman Sachs. Edward has broad experience across security engineering, risk management, critical infrastructure and system management and monitoring. It empowers operators to deploy, manage and distribute onchain strategies with unparalleled efficiency and risk controls.Risk ManagementStrategies on Makina have a defined mandate and risk parameters, that are enforced onchain.Advanced DeFi ExecutionPowered by the MakinaVM, offering full composability and atomicity, without the need for smart contract deployments.Cross-chainMakina enables secure and efficient deployment of funds across EVM compatible networks, offering operators unparalleled opportunities and users effortless access.Non-CustodialMakina allows users to get exposure to institutional-grade onchain strategies while always retaining custody of their assets.Makina is built for the era of agentic finance, empowering humans and agents alike to capture opportunities onchain securely and efficiently.MakinaFrequently asked questionsOverviewMachines & depositsSecurity & riskOverview01What is Makina?Makina is a next-generation DeFi Execution Engine that brings institutional-grade risk-adjusted strategies onchain. It enables capital allocators to deploy, manage, and automate complex financial strategies using programmable vaults called Machines, across chains.Makina also opens up access to a new class of curated yield opportunities for DeFi users, DAO treasuries, and retail depositors, allowing them to participate in strategies run by top-performing, professional operators that have historically been inaccessible or fragmented across chains.02Who is Makina for?Makina is built for professional strategists and DeFi-native users who need sophisticated onchain execution with robust risk controls.Makina is also for onchain participants, DAO Treasuries, and retail depositors seeking capital-efficient exposure to institutional-grade onchain strategies that were previously gated or off-chain. Makina lowers the barrier to access, offering a single interface to allocate into high-conviction, risk-managed opportunities, without needing to build the strategies yourself.03What makes Makina different?Makina offers a superior infrastructure for onchain strategies. These funds can be moved to Calibers that handle the execution of specific actions under defined rules.MachinesCalibers05What's the difference between a Machine and a Vault?A Vault is a general-purpose onchain container for capital and often limited in its ability to execute strategies. A Machine is an enhanced vault, representing a tokenized cross-chain strategy, with onchain risk controls and powered by a sophisticated execution engine.06How do I deposit into a Machine?To deposit into a Machine, users can either purchase Machine Tokens (MTs) on DEXs without KYC, or complete KYC and deposit directly into the Machine to mint Machine Tokens. All contracts underwent security audits from top-tier firms. Reports are publicly available in the technical documentation.ChainsecuritySigma PrimeOttersecCantina09What are the risks of using Makina?As with any DeFi protocol, using Makina carries risks, including potential smart contract vulnerabilities, bridge risks, risks linked to other DeFi protocols in which the strategy has positions, and market volatility. Makina mitigates these through multiple security audits, on-chain risk controls, and an emergency Recovery Mode. Client Diversity and Network Decentralisation For Ethereum | Nimbus Skip to main contentAbout NimbusCommunityGuideBlogJoin UsClient Diversity and Network Decentralisation For EthereumNimbus clientsDevelopment roadmapCore contributorsFAQContributor GuideSoftware LibrariesClient Diversity and Network Decentralisation For EthereumNimbus was created to promote client diversity and network decentralisation on Ethereum, believing that blockchain technology's full transformative potential can only be realised if running Ethereum infrastructure is widely accessible. Motivation​ Ethereum's security—its resistance to external threats and censorship—comes from its decentralisation. We believe that lowering the barrier to network participation will result in greater decentralisation and, consequently, a more resilient network. As such, we are building each of the three Nimbus clients to be as lightweight, secure, and easy to use as possible. The Nimbus consensus client, along with the still-in-development execution and light clients, is designed to perform on a range of systems, including Raspberry Pis and mobile devices, lowering the barrier to entry to run Ethereum's infrastructure. Meanwhile, our resource-conserving optimizations benefit those operating more powerful systems by freeing resources for other tasks without compromising on reward performance. Client projects that were earlier to the network than Nimbus have typically developed for higher specification hardware, as one would expect from the first client implementations. While these other implementations make for a more diverse client ecosystem, and their R&D efforts have pushed the space forward tremendously, there remains a gap for an Ethereum client tailored to lower specification devices that encourage increased network decentralisation while delivering the same level of stability and reward performance expected from any Ethereum client. Nimbus fills that gap. In addition to striving for maximum accessibility via lighter client implementations, Nimbus' design goals are to provide an architecture that makes it simple to embed Nimbus into other software. For example, the verified web3 proxy enables decentralised applications to verify data received from external RPC endpoints. Consequently, Nimbus reduces reliance on third-party software and service providers that introduce potential vulnerabilities through single points of failure. Nimbus history​ Status, the creator of the Ethereum-based decentralised messaging application, first announced Nimbus in August 2018 as a client implementation research project focused on sharding, light clients, and next-generation Ethereum technologies, with a goal of addressing scalability and accessibility concerns. It was inspired by a vision of the future in which Ethereum "lives" on millions of embedded systems around the world rather than a few thousand powerful computers. At its creation, Nimbus' goal was to research and build a client light enough to run on such resource-restricted devices, and modular enough to allow for rapid iteration and implementation of research. Initially, the team planned to develop an energy and compute-efficient, mobile-first client for the full web3 tech stack, with decentralised logic, decentralised storage, and decentralised messaging. However, as research into the latter two branches slowed, Nimbus narrowed its focus to crafting high-quality, lightweight Ethereum implementations to promote decentralisation and strengthen the network against single-client failures. Nomic Foundation | Empowering developers to decentralize the world◱◰◲◳Announcing the Nomic Foundation◱◰◳◲What we doJobsBlogHardhatSlangEDRTWITTERLINKEDINWhat we doJobsBlogHardhatSlangEDRTWITTERLINKEDINCareers at Nomic FoundationOur users are building the decentralized futureThe Nomic Foundation is a non-profit advancing the Ethereum ecosystem. We build runtimes, compilers, build systems, and deployment solutions that are used by tens of thousands of users. Our focus is on empowering developers to decentralize the world. You can help.See current openingsWhy join NomicYour impactAt Nomic, every person makes a difference. You will clearly see the impact that you contribute to our mission and Ethereum itself. Your team’s top-level results will be meaningfully different due to your contributions, and you will be able to pinpoint the exact contribution you made to upgrading a nascent industry’s stack.Deep technical challengesWe tackle deep developer infrastructure projects that are usually only available in larger organizations. We build runtimes and compilers used by tens of thousands of users.Mission-driven value creationYour contributions will directly impact an ecosystem that is shaping the future of finance, data, and ownership. You won’t be working on optimizing a revenue stream to increase shareholder profits; you’ll create value for the Ethereum community and developer ecosystem.Lean and robustWe run robust engineering practices and lightweight processes that provide us with structure and fast decision-making. Your time will be spent on technical challenges, coding, and launching features.Our valuesCrypto & Ethereum beliefWe believe in blockchain technology as a force for change that will produce meaningful value for society through innovation. We believe in Ethereum as a movement and technology, and we are aligned with its values. We actively participate in the community, and we aim to contribute to the long-term growth of the ecosystem.Social ImpactWe care about creating value for the world and Ethereum’s community in a meaningful way.Developer ExperienceWe consider a smooth building experience essential for ecosystem growth, and we take pride and pleasure in making software easier to build.Time is PreciousWe are respectful of people's time, including that of our users, the Ethereum community, external contributors, and our own team members and organization. Aiming for fast and efficient is our default.High StandardsWe aim to take the hard path without compromising quality or losing our sense of pragmatism.Level UpWe always try to improve at all levels: individually, in our projects, and as a team. Beginner's mindset.Instigate ChangeWhen we see room for improvement, we point it out and seek iteration, even if it's outside our direct responsibilities or areas of expertise.AutonomyTo create space for deep focus, schedule flexibility, and effective async remote collaboration, we strive for autonomy in how we approach work and collaboration.KindnessWe value and only hire people who embody respect, compassion, empathy, and kindness.CultureWe are an impact-driven remote team of 16 individuals coming from different walks of life. We look for alignment on mission and values as key aspects when we hire.Flexibility. Being able to work at any time, as long as I coordinate with my team, is super nice. Working alongside such a group of crazy smart people is really inspiring. It constantly reminds me that there’s so much to learn, and I love it.Luis Schaab,Software EngineerThe team is as welcoming as it is diverse, so whether it’s technical or cultural, I feel like I’m learning new things constantly which is really amazing.Zoey Morgan,Software EngineerWorking at a non-profit means being 100% focused on the value we are creating, which is great. And the team is amazing: smart, kind, and fun people, even if they don’t share enough pictures of their pets.Franco Victorio,Software EngineerRemote-firstOur team is fully remote, and we hire within UTC+2 to UTC-4 time zones. We work asynchronously and autonomously, relying on trust and great communication. This allows everyone to create a working schedule that integrates well with other important aspects of their lives. Hiring across many countries allows us to naturally integrate diverse perspectives.10 countries11 nationalities13 languagesTeam RetreatsWhile we love remote, time together in person is really important. Twice a year, we set aside about a week for our in-person retreats. We've had great times in places like Malaga, Patagonia, and Tuscany. During these trips we focus on work that’s well-suited for being in person, but we also have fun! Expect some hiking, yoga, kayaking, cooking, and even wine tasting. These retreats help us bond, share experiences, and build deeper relationships with one another.BenefitsRemote and flexible working arrangementsUnlimited PTOStipend to set up your home officeAnnual learning & development budgetVesting ETH package in your compJoin usOpen PositionsEngineering Hiring ProcessWeek 1Week 2ApplicationIntro callTechnical ScreenProject ReviewArchitectureCodingLeaderships InterviewsOfferReference ChecksFAQHow long does the interview process take?The core interviews take about 2 weeks, followed by the offer and reference checks stage.Which locations do you hire in?We hire within UTC+1 to UTC-4 time zones. Although we work asynchronously, hiring in these time zones allows for 3-4 hours of overlap between team members.How can I best prepare for interviewing with Nomic Foundation?If you’re reading this you’re on your way there! We encourage you to get familiar with Nomic and our core values. Additionally, looking into our open source projects will give you an idea of what we are building. Once you get invited to interview with us, our talent team will share more information about the interviews, what to expect, and how to prepare.How does Nomic manage remote work?We use Deel to employ team members internationally. Our workflow is based around asynchronous collaboration, relying heavily on written communication through Slack and Notion to maximize the time engineers spend on deep, uninterrupted, focused work. On Mondays, we kick off each week with a short team call. Every 2 weeks we schedule an unstructured team social, and we meet in person twice a year.How are the teams structured?Our teams are small, up to 4-5 people each. All engineers. We have team leads who also write code. The Engineering team is led by the Head of Engineering.What kind of development processes does the Engineering team follow?We loosely follow Scrum and OKRs for quarterly and yearly planning. Why is Nomic a non-profit?Ethereum has a need for meaningful effort on public goods, and the non-profit model allows for a clean set of incentives that align well with the interests of the ecosystem. In addition to that, the open-source projects we focus on aren’t great business opportunities. Organizations that build similar projects tend to be very large (big tech) and they do so to support their core businesses, rather than to make money off these projects. How is Nomic funded?We are backed by contributions from community members who recognize the essential role of developer experience in advancing Ethereum as a platform for software development.What is it like being a non-profit?It mirrors the early-stage tech startup world, but with different incentives, motivations, and definitions of non-financial success.How does being a non-profit influence goal setting and roadmap planning?The ultimate goal is impact and not profit, that’s the only difference. Poseidon runs that apprenticeship at industrial scale, with deep reach in Korea and across Asia.1.2The next generation of AI acts in the physical world. Its training data lives in people’s hands, in homes and factories, in the way work actually gets done. None of it can be scraped.1.3What little exists online rarely qualifies: footage without synchronized streams, distributions nobody controlled, activity staged for the camera. A model is only as good as the demonstrations it learns from.1.4Qualified footage is still not training data. It has to arrive model-ready: annotated for the reasoning behind each action, synchronized stream by stream, and packaged in the schema your pipeline expects. If your researchers spend weeks writing conversion scripts, the data was never model-ready.2.0 / Our productsPoseidon supplies qualified demonstration data in two forms: datasets you can evaluate today and custom collection to your spec.2.1The DatasetsExpert demonstration datasets across egocentric video, manipulation, and voice, collected in real homes, factories, and workplaces. We’re building a stablecoin clearinghouse. The clearinghouse connects stablecoin issuers to fintechs, banks, neobanks and other businesses building with stablecoins. It brings fungibility to stablecoins, so companies can build products knowing stablecoins can always be sendable or spendable worth exactly $1, just like they can with fiat dollars.What is a clearinghouse?Clearinghouses solve a fundamental coordination problem. They transform a fragmented many-to-many market into a unified network: individual participants can interact with one counterparty and reach the rest of the network.Why do stablecoins need a clearinghouse?Stablecoin users need to coordinate money movement across any GENIUS-bill compliant stablecoin, but it’s not feasible to have a direct relationship with every issuer. With our stablecoin clearinghouse, clients can access all supported stablecoins in the same way the banks use ACH (a bank clearinghouse) to transfer money to all other member banks.How is it different from the existing stablecoin infrastructure that currently exists?Existing infrastructure is built for trading, not payments. That means moving between stablecoins typically requires a trade or spot transaction: stablecoins are valued at a market price which is often not exactly $1. Our clearinghouse is purpose-built for payments and settlement with no market-based transaction so stablecoins move at exactly $1.Who is the clearinghouse designed for?We built it from first principles for payment use cases. Our platform is designed for fintechs, neobanks, payment companies, and any business that wants stablecoin payment products that are faster, cheaper, and more seamless.What stablecoins can The Better Money Company support?The TBMC clearinghouse will support any GENIUS-compliant stablecoin. Our engineers support the technological advancement of the Tezos blockchain by working on the technological core - its protocol.View open rolesCommercialOur commercial teams work with creators, entrepreneurs, brands, organizations and technologists to support the building of projects on the Tezos Blockchain and develop commercial solutions.View open rolesIt's a really stimulating environment to work in: I go home buzzing from all the new things I've learned.Emma Turner, Software EngineerDiscover Want to learn more about the world we work in? Start discovering the basics belowWhat is a blockchain?A blockchain is essentially a technical framework in which digital transactions are agreed upon without central authority, recorded in an unchangeable ledger, and maintained across a network of computers. As fresh data is added to the network, a new ‘block’ is created and attached to the ‘chain’. It's essentially innovative database technology that is transforming how we exchange value. There are public and private blockchains; public blockchains are ledgers of information on global, decentralised networks.What are blockchains used for?Though blockchains differ in their design and technical features, most of them support two key functionalities: transacting value in the form of cryptocurrencies, and executing instructions called smart contracts. Smart contracts, in turn, provide the foundation for decentralized applications, also known as dapps.What is Tezos?Tezos is an open-source, self-upgrading blockchain built to last.By design, Tezos embraces long-term upgradability, open participation, collaboration, and smart contract safety. Its on-chain governance lets stakeholders deliver protocol upgrades without disruptive hard forks, so applications stay stable while the network keeps getting faster and more capable. Tezos continuously and seamlessly upgrades itself, adding the latest innovations to deliver novel and new capabilities within the space.The original proof-of-stake protocol, Tezos now offers a sub-50ms latency EVM layer, a native data availability layer, and rollups to scale serious applications. Since 2018, Tezos has processed hundreds of millions of transactions representing billions of dollars in value, powering tokenized finance, gaming, and digital ownership for a global community.What is decentralized finance (DeFi)?DeFi is short for “decentralized finance,” which is an umbrella term for a variety of financial applications in cryptocurrency or blockchain geared toward disrupting financial intermediaries.What is an NFT?NFT stands for Non-Fungible Token.“Non-fungible” means that it is completely unique. “Token” means that it can be transferred on a blockchain. Essentially, NFTs are assets that carry a unique digital identity and can be traded between users on a public blockchain like Tezos. Common examples of NFTs include artwork, trading cards, comic books, sports collectibles, games and more. Although NFTs tend to be associated with artwork, they actually represent much more.What is a crypto wallet?A crypto wallet is an application or device that functions as a wallet for your cryptocurrency and makes the blockchain accessible to everyone. It allows you to store and transfer cryptocurrency. It provides the interface that lets you access your crypto and stores the passkeys you use to sign for your cryptocurrency. Wallets contain a public key (the wallet address) and your private keys needed to sign cryptocurrency transactions. Anyone who knows the private key can control the coins associated with that address. There are various types of wallets, with its own features and security levels. How environmentally friendly is Tezos?Tezos, as a pioneering layer 1 Proof-of-Stake blockchain, has always been recognized as an energy-efficient alternative to more traditional Proof of Work blockchains. typeRemoteEmployment typeFull timeApply for this role (opens in a new tab)See all open rolesBuild a Safer World.TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.The Sales Enablement Manager for Onchain Compliance equips TRM’s go-to-market team to sell compliance solutions with consistency and credibility in a fast-moving regulatory market. You will design and continuously improve the onboarding, training, certification, and coaching that shorten time to productivity for the field, and you will run enablement as an AI-first system so a small team can scale as TRM’s products and processes change. This role sits at the center of TRM’s GTM engine, partnering closely with Sales Leadership, PMM, Product, and Deployment.The impact you will have:Shorten time-to-ramped-productivity for the Onchain Compliance GTM team by owning segment-specific onboarding built as an AI-first system, using AI to turn a product spec into a full enablement package, including a knowledge check, in a single working session.Keep the field credible the moment the market moves by building training, roleplays, and talk tracks from real call and deal data with AI, so the team can speak to new capabilities and regulatory events fast.Raise win rates by running ongoing training and certification across discovery, product mastery, objection handling, competitive positioning, and compliance fundamentals, with AI-generated roleplays and call analysis pinpointing where each person needs practice.Help managers develop their teams by delivering AI-driven personalized development paths for each GTM team member and surfacing the coaching signals that matter most.Protect the field from risk by building AI quality checks so nothing inaccurate on compliance or regulation reaches a customer conversation.Scale a small team’s reach by building and shipping your own agents and automations without waiting on RevOps or engineering, automating last quarter’s manual work every quarter.What we’re looking World offers universal Proof of Human, finance and connection for every human.World Foundation (Foundation), for its part, is the initial steward of the protocol. Its mandate is to support and grow World to self-sufficiency. It does this by facilitating decentralization over time, consistent with the mission and commitments of World. In practical terms, the Foundation may contribute by defining protocol governance, token mechanisms, grant programs, community affairs and more. The Foundation provides direction for the services Tools for Humanity performs in relation to the protocol...Is World available in the United States?Yes. World App is available in the United States. People in the United States (with the exception of the State of New York) can verify their World ID, access the full World App experience, and choose to claim WLD. What is Tools for Humanity and what is its relation to World?Tools for Humanity (TFH) is a technology company building for humans in the age of AI, with its headquarters in San Francisco and Munich, and a wholly-owned subsidiary in Bavaria, Germany. TFH took the initial steps toward developing the protocol and supported its multi-year beta testing phase. It then transitioned the protocol to the independent World Foundation prior to the protocol’s launch in late July 2023. TFH will continue to develop important tools supporting World and beyond.Today, TFH provides services to World Foundation. Those services include, for example, software development, hardware manufacturing and market operations logistical support. TFH is governed entirely separately from World Foundation.Who owns Tools for Humanity?Tools for Humanity is a privately-held technology company building for humans in the age of AI. Co-founded by Sam Altman, Alex Blania and Max Novendstern in 2019, it is funded by investors including venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz, Bain Capital Crypto, Blockchain Capital, and Khosla Ventures. The technology company is headquartered in San Francisco. Sam Altman serves as the company’s chairman and Alex Blania as its CEO. Tools for Humanity is currently building tools for World.How is World addressing the environmental impact of blockchains and crypto assets?World is built on the Ethereum blockchain utilizing both layer 1 and layer 2 technologies for efficiency. On September 15, 2022 the Ethereum blockchain underwent “the merge,” a transition that reduced the energy used in operating the Ethereum blockchain by more than 99.95% overnight. For more information on the merge, please see Ethereum’s blog.How do I stay up-to-date on the latest World developments?The best ways to receive the latest information about World are to download World App, subscribe to email updates, or follow World on X or Discord. Updates are also available via the blog.Where can I go to learn about opportunities to work on World?Because World is an open source protocol, it is supported by a global community of developers, individuals, economists and technologists. Anyone can use their skills to contribute to World, by engaging on World GitHub, building a Mini App, becoming a World Operator or Community Operator, or pursuing a grant from World Foundation. Each time a crypto asset is acquired, mined or received for a profit, the gains automatically qualify as capital gains. According to the IRS, crypto assets are treated as property and hence, are taxable. So your capital gains will also be taxed accordingly and are known as capital gains tax. Capital gains can be calculated using the formula:Capital Gains = Selling Price – Purchase Price (Cost Basis)Calculate your crypto taxes for free from our crypto tax calculator tool How do you avoid tax on crypto? There is no way that you can avoid paying crypto taxes to the IRS. However, you can minimize your tax obligations in a few ways. If your losses outweigh your gains, you can offset $3,000 of income, as well as take advantage of the lack of wash sale rule using tax-loss harvesting. How much taxes do you pay on crypto profit? The rate of tax on your crypto profits depends on two crucial factors: the holding period of the assets and income brackets. Based on the holding period, crypto gains can be of two types. Short-term capital gains taxes, where assets are held less than a year and the rates range from 10% to 37%. Next are long-term capital gains taxes, in which the assets are held for over a year before selling them. In this case, the rate of taxes ranges from 0% to 20%, depending on your income. Do you need to report crypto gains? Cryptocurrency is taxed the same way as property. So whenever you’re disposing of an asset for another asset, you’ll be liable to pay taxes, based on the transaction that you carry out. Your transaction can be categorized into two types of taxable events: capital gains taxes and income taxes. And again, there are some transactions that are tax-free. So, depending on the transaction you’ll have to report your crypto gains to the IRS. Is crypto tax software safe? Crypto tax software helps you by tracking, managing, and calculating the gains or losses on your crypto transactions. Your funds are not accessible through crypto tax software, they are read-only, so this keeps your assets safe from hacks or theft. How can ZenLedger help? ZenLedger is the best crypto tax software. Stablecoins are digital currencies designed to maintain a stable value, typically pegged to fiat currencies like the U.S. dollar. Digital asset infrastructure refers to the technology systems that allow financial institutions to interact with blockchain networks and digital assets. web3Evidence.text: Zodl — Zcash-powered mobile wallet. Skip to content Home About Blog Download Zcash-powered mobile wallet bringing unstoppable private money to billions Download Built for Financial Sovereignty PrivacyUnlike most apps that claim to prioritize privacy, Zodl is actually built for it. Designed for shielded Zcash, best-in-class privacy is in its DNA. Self-CustodyOnly you can see, access, and manage your wallet. You are in complete control of your funds. No gatekeepers. Your keys, your crypto. ConsentFor us, informed choice is a first-class principle. We give you the information you need to understand your options and make decisions. You don’t need to know how blockchains work to use private money. Zodl hides the complexity while holding the line on security. It’s an easy, low-risk way to get started with Zcash or explore crypto for the first time. Download Get Ready to Zodl ZEC-to-ZEC Payments The most private way to transact, period. Zcash is the most private cryptocurrency ever designed, and Zodl is built by a team of battle-tested mobile engineers and Zcash core protocol developers, uniquely equipped to honor that design. Shielded Zcash keeps transaction details hidden on the blockchain, and Zodl extends that protection at the wallet level. CrossPay Make private cross-chain payments. Just because your friends expose their financial data on public blockchains, doesn’t mean you should. With Zodl CrossPay, you send shielded ZEC from Zodl, and they get paid in the asset they prefer, like BTC or a stablecoin. Stay private. Onboard them later. Swaps Swap to and from shielded ZEC. Zodl’s built-in private swaps are the simplest, most privacy-preserving way to fund your Zodl wallet or swap ZEC into another cryptocurrency. Powered by NEAR Intents, this feature connects Zcash to other crypto ecosystems without relying on centralized exchanges. Cold Storage Store shielded ZEC in a hardware wallet. Keystone is the first hardware wallet to support shielded ZEC. This air-gapped device gives your Zcash an extra layer of security. Connect it to Zodl to manage your Keystone funds through our app. Use the hardware wallet to sign outgoing transactions inside Zodl. This is self-custody done right. Real-World Purchases Pay with Zcash at thousands of retail locations. Use Zodl to pay major merchants like GameStop, Sheetz, Chipotle, and more without turning your personal information over to faceless data brokers who buy and sell your data without your knowledge or consent. Zodl shields your data. Flexa handles the checkout. You get less spam and a reduced risk of fraud. No Tracking We go out of our way to know nothing about you. Zodl does not collect, track, or see your wallet activity. We don't use analytics to observe your in-app behavior. We don’t have access to your transaction history, balances, clicks and habits, or personal data. We don’t profile. To fix bugs, we only use industry-standard anonymized crash reports and cannot tie that data to specific users. 1-Click Shielding Privacy starts with shielding. We made it easy. While Zodl is built for shielded ZEC, it can still receive transparent (unshielded) ZEC as an on-ramp from centralized exchanges that tend to lag on privacy and not make the effort to support shielded ZEC. When a transparent balance is detected, Zodl prompts you to shield it with a single tap. Once your funds are shielded, they can be used for private payments. Shielded Notes Zcash-level privacy for your messages. Zcash supports encrypted shielded notes, allowing private messages to be sent alongside transactions or on their own. Attach a private note to a payment or send a private message on its own by setting the transaction amount to zero. The note will be visible only to you and your recipient. Built by Zcash OGs Created by the original inventors and developers of the Zcash protocol, who set the standard for on-chain privacy, together with the product team that redefined Zcash UX, unlocking ZEC’s potential. About Zcash Open Development Lab (ZODL) - Zodl Skip to content Home About Blog Download Our Why We envision a world without mass financial surveillance, where law⁠-⁠abiding people can transact freely and privately, without fear that their data will be exploited, sold, or weaponized by criminals, corporations, or governments. A world where financial privacy is the default and access to markets is a human right. Because the ability to make transactions that sustain life and liberty should belong to everyone. There is no sovereignty without privacy. Onward About Our Work Zcash Protocol Core Zcash protocol development that began at Electric Coin Company has moved to ZODL, Zcash Open Development Lab. The engineers who designed, implemented, and maintained Zcash’s most critical systems continue that work here with the same commitment and integrity the ecosystem has relied on for years. Zcash is decentralized and developed by multiple teams. We work alongside them across the growing ecosystem. Zcash UX The team that built and launched the flagship Zcash wallet Zashi at Electric Coin Company (ECC) left ECC and formed a new company, Zcash Open Development Lab (ZODL). Zashi is now Zodl, and the ZODL team continues to develop the wallet. There is no action required from the wallet users. The rebrand from Zashi to Zodl happens automatically with the latest app update, with no impact on the user experience. Open-source development Our work is open-source because reliable financial privacy requires transparent development. Anyone can inspect our protocol code, audit our wallet, and verify our work. This is foundational to user sovereignty. You should be able to review, rebuild, or fork the software you rely on. That’s how control stays with users, instead of platforms or builders. We don’t ask for trust. We show our work. Security & Innovation ZODL’s core engineers are the original creators of Zcash, with a level of cryptography and protocol mastery unmatched by any other Zcash wallet team. This allows the Zodl wallet product team to innovate with a full understanding of the blockchain’s requirements, capabilities, potential, and risks. Our wallet feels simple on the surface, but is powered by engineering depth other wallets simply don’t reach. Get Support Download Your Email Subscribe Swiss banks wish.
